name: Sagility
desc:
Credentialing Advocate | $16.00 – $20.00 per hour + performance-based incentives
You spend your day verifying healthcare providers’ licenses, education, board certifications, and work history by contacting primary sources, keeping their records accurate and up to date in the credentialing system, tracking expiration dates so nothing lapses, and preparing complete files for review. When something is missing or doesn’t match, you reach out to the provider to get the right paperwork and clear up discrepancies. You also help with audits, answer internal and external questions about credentialing status, and make sure everything stays compliant. In short, you’re the person making sure doctors and other providers are properly credentialed so they can keep seeing patients.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education minimum: High school diploma or equivalent
Required experience: Minimum of 6 months at a single employer (preferably healthcare or customer service); strong attention to detail and organizational skills
Preferred experience: Previous administrative, healthcare operations, or data entry experience in a healthcare setting; familiarity with credentialing software or provider databases (MP3, Echo, NOW, CAQH, etc.); basic understanding of healthcare compliance or regulatory requirements
Required skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook); strong written and verbal communication; ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines; ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information; reliable attendance (no absences during the first 90 days)
This role is ideal for someone who:
Is highly detail-oriented and enjoys checking documents for accuracy
Likes organized, process-driven work with clear standards and deadlines
Communicates professionally and follows up consistently with providers and internal teams
Wants a stable work-from-home role in healthcare operations with room to grow
Who is not a good fit:
Someone who gets bored with repetitive documentation and data-entry tasks
Anyone who struggles with strict attention to detail or meeting deadlines
People who prefer constant fast-paced interaction over focused, independent work
Those who cannot maintain a quiet, private home workspace with reliable hardwired internet
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
Application
Expect an assessment (skills or detail-oriented test) at the end of the application or emailed shortly after
If the assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or phone for a phone screen
If the phone screen passes, expect a final interview (typically video)
Total time to hire from date of application can typically range from 1 to 3 weeks depending on volume and scheduling.
Most Likely Interview Questions:
Tell me about a time you had to manage multiple deadlines or priorities. How did you stay organized and ensure accuracy?
Describe a situation where you found an error or discrepancy in documentation. What steps did you take to resolve it?
How do you handle sensitive or confidential information, and why is that important in a role like this?
This position requires frequent follow-up with providers to collect missing documents. How comfortable are you with professional outreach and persistence?
Tell me about your experience with Microsoft Excel or data entry. How do you ensure high accuracy when working with detailed records?
Top 10 Resume Keywords to Stand Out:
Credentialing / recredentialing
Primary source verification
Provider records management
Healthcare compliance
Attention to detail
Document tracking & expiration monitoring
Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook)
Data entry accuracy
Confidentiality & sensitive information handling
Multi-priority deadline management

Career Pathway (5 growth paths this role can lead to):
Senior Credentialing Advocate / Specialist – handling more complex files and mentoring new team members
Credentialing Team Lead / Supervisor – overseeing a small team and owning quality metrics
Provider Enrollment or Network Operations Coordinator – expanding into broader provider onboarding and network management
Compliance / Quality Assurance Analyst – focusing on audits, regulatory readiness, and process improvement
Operations Manager or Client Services Lead – moving into leadership roles that manage larger teams or client relationships (many leaders at Sagility started in entry-level positions like this)
